l.i: Una Eurus, Zephyrúsque, Notus Boreasq; furentes Disjciunt laceram, quassamq; euertere puppim Certatim incumbunt, nisi me tua dextera præsens Defensum daret, atque animum in discrimine forte, Sufficeretq; nouas vires mihi, maxime Christe?

Hinc mea perpetuis exercet pectora curis Perfidus humani generis fraudator & hostis, Impia terribiles acuens in prælia reges, Et coniuratos cælum rescindere ferro, Si possint, si Christe sinas: quo scilicet omnis, Execranda bonis, nullo prohibente, tyranni Romani probet, & mendacia mundus adoret: Ni faciant, ferrum, carcerq; timendus, & ignis, Sanguineq; innocuo campiq; urbesq; replenda, Interea toto cultus divinus in orbe, Veraq; religio tenebris tristiq; premantur Nocte, nec in terris, qui Christi nomen honoret, Sit quisquam, sed quod cantato pollinis orbi Fingitur inclusum, & miseri mortalibus ævi Per vim, perq; nefas obtruditur, illud inane Idolum placeat, vigeat, solumq; colatur, Et varia fraudum species, horrendaq; trini Unius Dei passim ludibria regnent.

Illinc luctifico mæstam mihi vulnere mentem Sauciat, heu patriæ nostræ communis Erinnys, Turcus in Ungaricos grassans crudeliter agros, Omnia ubi ferro latè populatur & igni, Christicolumq; nimis sitiens Otmanna cruorem Barbaries, diroq; parans molimine Eoi

page.notes: Verse set in italic with long s rendered as plain s. The q with a superscript hook is transcribed as q; for -que. The catchword "Finibus" is at the lower right and is kept separate from the text. The verse in the first and third paragraphs is indented on its opening line, which marks the stanza breaks. Several words carry faint printed marks over the vowels and could not be confirmed letter by letter, but they were read as shown.
